solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Moving letters: Dear Elle, where's Del?

indicators.note: letters that are moved about end up in a new order, so the words that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: An agony-aunt letter to Elle asking where Del has gone, with a note that it is moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Del is Del Boy Trotter of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, a market trader always chasing a dodgy deal; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Del Boy is the archetypal sharp, scheming small-time trader, an example of the type the answer names.

clue.text: Match injury unsettled, about to become terminally gangrenous

blocks.note: harm is damage or injury
surface padding: it colours the wound picture and supplies no letters in this reading
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
'to be' gives IS, and the terminal letter of become adds the last letter
surface padding: it completes the medical picture and supplies no letters

explanation.surface: A wound left untreated is getting worse and is on the point of turning gangrenous.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: only injury, about and the end of 'to become' seem to supply letters; 'unsettled' and 'gangrenous' read as surface colour. The parse here is a best reading, not a certain one.
explanation.definitionFit: To harmonise colours or styles is to make them go together, which is to match them.

clue.text: A hairy man's slice of veggie sausage

indicators.note: a slice is a piece cut out of something larger, so the letters are cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A bearded man eating a slice of meat-free sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Jacob says 'Esau my brother is a hairy man'; the phrase is a standard crossword route to the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible describes Esau, Jacob's twin brother, as hairy, so he is the hairy man of scripture.

clue.text: One Pole following straightforward German writing about border flower

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the writing goes round the border
following puts the one and the pole after the straightforward word

blocks.note: an even path is level and simple
the Roman numeral for one
N for north pole
G is the abbreviation for German
prose is ordinary written language
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A Polish writer living abroad after a plain-spoken German author wrote about a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening primrose is a yellow-flowered plant whose blooms open at dusk.

clue.text: Blue Peter and Jolly Roger may express conflicting principles

blocks.note: first meaning: two ships' flags, a pair of standards
second meaning: one rule for some and another rule for others

explanation.surface: A children's TV show and a pirate emblem can stand for contradictory values.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Peter is the flag a ship flies when about to sail (also a long-running UK children's TV show); the Jolly Roger is the pirate flag. A standard is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Double standards are inconsistent rules applied differently to different people, so principles that conflict.

clue.text: I help along foreign admirer of English

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An overseas visitor offering assistance because they love the English.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglophile is someone with a great fondness for England and English culture.

clue.text: Prince always tours Maine

indicators.note: to tour is to go all the way round, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A royal who is forever on tour in a New England state.
explanation.walkthrough: The always-word splits as E...ER around the state.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, more often spelt emir, is a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Vintage clothing to begin with is rubbish

blocks.note: garb is clothing
a wine's vintage is its age or year

explanation.surface: Second-hand designer clothes dismissed as junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to begin with' tells you the clothing comes first, ahead of the vintage word.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is waste, the American word for household refuse.

clue.text: Clothes stand

blocks.note: first meaning: an outfit, especially an odd one
second meaning: to rise to your feet

explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen and space differ: the noun for an outfit is hyphenated, the verb for standing is two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is an outfit someone wears, and to get up is to rise and stand.

clue.text: A French man bottling universal ointment

indicators.note: bottling something holds it inside, so one piece is kept within another

blocks.note: un is French for a
a gent is a man
U is the film rating for universal

explanation.surface: A Frenchman keeping a jar of all-purpose cream.
explanation.definitionFit: An unguent is a soothing or healing salve, a word for an ointment.

clue.text: Inventor set up US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An inventor established in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the inventor behind alternating-current electrical systems.

clue.text: Gun – rifle – pointing the wrong way

indicators.note: something pointing the wrong way faces backwards, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: to rifle a place is to loot it

explanation.surface: A firearm aimed back at the person holding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like the gun, but it is the verb; Gun is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tool is slang for a handgun in criminal talk, as in 'tooled up'.

clue.text: More than one hoarding banknotes, getting fed up I hear

indicators.note: what I hear is a spoken version, so the answer matches the phrase by sound

blocks.note: bills are American banknotes, and bored means fed up

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiling cash grows tired of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' looks like stockpiling money, but in Britain a hoarding is a large outdoor advertising board.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarding is the British word for an advertising board, so several of them are billboards.

clue.text: Perhaps ironic and self-referential leader crossing Old Street, on about communist uprising

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across, so the leader spans the old street and holds it inside
in a down clue an uprising reads from the bottom up, so the communist is backwards
on goes about, round the outside of the reversed communist

blocks.note: PM is the Prime Minister, the national leader
O is the abbreviation for old
St is the abbreviation for Street
taken as written
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A political leader walking across Old Street during a communist revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Street is a real London road; here it is just O and ST inside the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Irony and self-reference are hallmarks of the late-twentieth-century movement in art and literature, so these are typical features of it.

clue.text: Chlorine in Italian river and air around island, in whatever proportion

indicators.note: ingredients combined in whatever proportion go together in any mixture, so the pieces need not stay in clue order

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
air is a gas
on means about, which is around
Is is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A chemist describing chlorine in an Italian river mixing with the air over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces simply line up as river, island, around, air: the last phrase frees them from clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Chlorine was used as a chemical weapon in the First World War, an example of a toxic battlefield vapour.

clue.text: Wild animal without name is heavy set? Not very

indicators.note: not very tells you to take away the letter standing for very
set as in a bone being reset, so the letters are put into a new position

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Asking whether a beast lacking a name is heavily built, and answering not really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavy set' looks like one phrase meaning stocky; set is in fact the shuffle signal once very is gone from heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a scavenging carnivore of the African plains, so a kind of wild beast.

clue.text: Well-designed, or coming unstuck after initial experimentation?

indicators.note: coming unstuck means falling apart, so the letters break up and re-form
initial points to the first letter only

blocks.note: the first letter of experimentation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a product is well built or falls apart after the first trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic describes something shaped for efficient, comfortable use by the human body.

clue.text: A W-H-E-A-T?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cereal named letter by letter
setter's reading: the word is written out letter by letter, which is the past tense of to spell, and also an ancient cereal

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses at once: the hyphenated letters show a word spelt out, and the answer is also an old variety of grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt is an ancient species of grain, and also the past participle of the verb for naming letters in order.

clue.text: It is, in short, an exercise!

blocks.note: surface reading: a remark, briefly put, that something is an exercise
setter's reading: the shortened form of it is, written upward in this down light, describes the answer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tis is the short form of it is; written bottom to top in a down light, it reads the answer's first word, and the second word says the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is a gym move raising the trunk from lying to sitting, strengthening the stomach.

clue.text: Correct to embrace nobleman – retrospectively this is illuminating

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms round, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: right means correct
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A historian deciding it is right to embrace an aristocrat, finding the view in hindsight enlightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' looks like hindsight but means at the back: the definition is a lamp facing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle's tail lamp shines from the back, so it gives light to the rear.

clue.text: Idiot heads to town when everyone remains put

indicators.note: heads are the tops, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A fool who heads into town when everybody else is staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly, annoying person, an informal word for a fool.

clue.text: Bespoke leotard I am altering

indicators.note: altering changes something's form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dressmaker explaining she is taking in a custom-made leotard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bespoke clothing is made to an individual's measurements, as a tailor would cut it.

clue.text: Watch Sirius somewhat to the north of Hibernia

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase, so the letters sit inside it
in a down clue, heading north means reading from the bottom up

blocks.note: the letters span the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Stargazing advice: look at the Dog Star a little north of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernia is the Latin name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernia is the classical Latin name for Ireland, so belonging to it means from that country.

clue.text: Fixed stake in volcano, facing west

indicators.note: in an across answer, west is leftward, so the word runs right to left

blocks.note: Etna is the volcano on Sicily

explanation.surface: A post driven into a volcano's flank, pointing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stake' suggests a post, but it is a gambling stake.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the set amount each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Fine tune and clean

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Instructions to adjust an instrument and polish it.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine is itself a meaning of the answer too, as in fair weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair copy is a clean one, and fair play is clean, honest play.

clue.text: Textbook on old, old card game

blocks.note: a primer is an elementary textbook
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A reference book about a historic card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated old is no typo: the first gives a letter, the second starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Primero was a gambling game with cards, popular in Tudor England.

clue.text: Plan to wander around Germany with a priest

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the wander word is placed round the country

blocks.note: to roam is to wander
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: An itinerary for touring Germany in a clergyman's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A road map figuratively means a strategy setting out the steps toward a goal.

clue.text: Shocked to be beneath small lorry on Thursday

blocks.note: Th is the abbreviation for Thursday
under means beneath
S is the abbreviation for small
a lorry is a truck

explanation.surface: Horrified at finding oneself trapped under a little lorry one Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on Thursday' puts the day's letters first; lorry is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thunderstruck is to be stunned with amazement, as if hit by a thunderbolt.
